# Snowflake (apify/snowflake)

The Apify actor [`apify/snowflake-apify-snowflake`](https://apify.com/apify/snowflake-apify-snowflake) as typed Telo kinds, generated from its default build **0.0.1** (module version **0.1.0**). Runs use whatever build the actor has as default when they start, so they keep working as Apify retires old builds; the input types below are refreshed weekly and can lag an actor that changed its input since.

Imports any Apify dataset into a Snowflake table with append or create modes. Supports custom column mapping, automatic table creation with schema inference, batching, resumable imports, and programmatic access token (PAT) authentication. Works standalone or as an Actor-to-Actor integration.

## Pricing

Free — you pay only for the Apify platform usage (compute units) of the run.

Runs are charged to the Apify account whose token the `ApifyClient` holds. See the [Store page](https://apify.com/apify/snowflake-apify-snowflake) for current prices.

## Import

```yaml
imports:
  Actor: oci://ghcr.io/telorun/apify/apify-snowflake-apify-snowflake@0.1.0#sha256-…
```

Pin the digest with `telo upgrade`. The module re-exports `ApifyClient`, so it is the only import needed.

## Usage

```yaml
kind: Actor.ApifyClient
metadata: { name: apify }
token: !cel "secrets.apifyToken"
---
kind: Actor.Run          # or Actor.Start for runs longer than 5 minutes
metadata: { name: scrape }
client: !ref apify
maxTotalChargeUsd: 1     # optional: timeout, memory, maxItems, maxTotalChargeUsd
---
kind: Run.Sequence
metadata: { name: main }
steps:
  - name: scrape
    invoke: !ref scrape
    inputs:
      datasetId: "…"
```

- **`Run`** calls Apify's synchronous endpoint and returns `{ items }`. Apify holds the request open for at most 300 seconds; a longer run fails with HTTP 408.
- **`Start`** starts the run, long-polls it until it finishes, and returns `{ run, items }`. A run that ends `FAILED`, `TIMED-OUT` or `ABORTED` raises `APIFY_RUN_NOT_SUCCEEDED` with the run as `data`.

## Input

Only these fields are accepted — `telo check` rejects any other.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `datasetId` | string | yes |  | Dataset — Usually the default dataset of an Actor or task run. To import each run of another Actor, set it to `{{resource.defaultDatasetId}}` in that Actor's integration. |
| `snowflakeAccount` | string | yes |  | Account identifier — Uses `orgname-accountname` format, like `myorg-myaccount`. Go to Snowflake -> Your Account -> Connect a tool to Snowflake -> Account identifier, or run `SELECT CURRENT_ORGANIZATION_NAME() \|\| '-' \|\| CURRENT_ACCOUNT_NAME();`. |
| `snowflakeUsername` | string | yes |  | Login name — Go to Snowflake -> Your Account -> Connect a tool to Snowflake -> Login name, or run `DESCRIBE USER ;` with the name from `SELECT CURRENT_USER();` and copy `LOGIN_NAME`. |
| `snowflakePat` | string | yes |  | Programmatic access token — Go to Snowflake -> Your Account -> Settings -> Authentication -> Programmatic access tokens and generate one, or run `ALTER USER ADD PROGRAMMATIC ACCESS TOKEN ;` in Snowflake. Snowflake shows the token only once. |
| `snowflakeWarehouse` | string |  |  | Warehouse — Leave empty to use your default warehouse. Required if you don't have one. To check, run `SELECT CURRENT_WAREHOUSE();` in Snowflake. |
| `importMode` | string | yes | `"append"` | Import mode — Both options add rows and never replace data. Create new table (`create_new`) also creates a missing table. |
| `destination` | object | yes |  | Destination table — Snowflake table to write into. With Exact names on, matching is case-sensitive. Names are uppercase by default. To check, run a `SHOW` command. Browse what you can access in Snowsight's Databases explorer, Snowflake's web interface. |
| `columnMapping` | object[] |  | `[]` | Column mapping — Import only these fields, under these column names, in either mode. Leave empty to import every field in the first 5,000 rows. A source field missing from the dataset imports as an empty column. |
| `quoteIdentifiers` | boolean |  | `true` | Exact names — When on, database, schema, table, and column names keep their case and special characters. Names must match exactly. Names with lowercase letters, spaces, or special characters need double quotes in queries. When off, names are uppercase and unquoted, and column names can only use lett |

## Output

The actor publishes no dataset schema, so `items` are untyped objects.
